newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Phillips -- insurance, securities not risky.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Phillips -- insurance, securities not risky.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips said Monday securities and insurance activities are generally no more risky than regular bank activities.

"Except for some types of insurance underwriting, these activities are generally no more risky, and often significantly less risky, than many activities in which banks routinely engage -- namely, lending," she said.
In a speech prepared for a banking seminar, she said banking laws "severely restrict" banking-related activities of securities and insurance underwriting and dealing.
Phillips added that the Federal Reserve Board is trying to give banks as much leeway as current law allows.
"Although I remain hopeful that Congress will address some of these issues, we at the Board are trying to provide banks as much latitude, commensurate with risk, that existing laws allow," she said.
